$comment: Derived copy of docs/design/tokens.json, bundled for runtime resource access in ExactMacConsole. docs/design/tokens.json is the authoritative single source of truth for design tokens. docs/design.fig is the design of record and drawn contract, holding zero variables as a known toolchain limit.

color.$comment: Semantic names, never gray-NNN. Red is reserved for deny and high-risk emphasis, amber for caution and expiry, green only for an active grant. Light and dark are the same names with different values, which is what makes a single SwiftUI semantic color possible. Every text color meets WCAG AA (4.5:1) on its own scheme's surface AND on surface-raised and surface-sunken, because components place text on all three: Apple's stock #86868B tertiary measures 3.62:1 on white, and #B25000 caution measured 4.37:1 on sunken, so tertiary is darkened to clear AA on all three surfaces (#68686D light, #949499 dark) and caution to #A04A00. This class of bug bit THREE times, and the first two fixes were both wrong: the first pass validated only against `surface`, and the second pass fixed only the combinations that happened to be used, leaving light/success at 4.23:1 on sunken and dark/danger at 4.09:1 on raised. Claiming compliance without a check was the actual defect. The rule is now mechanically ENFORCED by automated tests against tokens.json asserting every text token clears 4.5:1 on surface, surface-raised or surface-sunken in either scheme, and on-accent clears 4.5:1 on accent. success is #1A753F and danger dark is #FF5E52 for exactly this reason. accent FAILED this test as small text on a tinted surface (3.84:1 on sunken), so its two jobs are split: `accent` is a FILL, `accent-text` is INK, and `on-accent` is the label colour that sits on an accent fill. No single blue can do both jobs in dark mode, where the constraint inverts: #3D8BFF gives white-on-fill 3.31:1 but ink-on-raised 4.20:1, and every lighter blue trades one for the other. `on-accent` is dark ink in dark mode, which is why the primary button's label is not hardcoded white. Apple's stock #86868B tertiary measures 3.62:1 and #7C7C81 measures 4.10:1, so tertiary is darkened to the system label grays. separator is a decorative hairline and is deliberately below 3:1; control-border is the one used for interactive edges, which must be perceivable.

space.$comment: 4pt grid. space-1 is the base step; 8 and above are the primary rhythm used for section separation.

type.$comment: PRODUCTION is SF Pro for prose and Menlo for anything the machine will execute or reported; the app maps to these at build time. THE .FIG CANNOT RENDER EITHER, and this is a recorded toolchain limit, not a choice: `openpencil fonts` reports Inter as the only available family and substitutes Courier New, DejaVu Sans, DejaVu Sans Mono, Menlo and Roboto all to Inter. So the design has ONE face and NO monospace. The weight ladder below is real and available (Regular, Medium, SemiBold, Bold), and the exact spelling matters absolutely: ONLY 'Semi Bold' with a space is honoured. 'SemiBold', 'Semibold', 'semibold' and ' DemiBold' are ALL silently downgraded to Regular, so a whole design rendered at one weight while claiming a four-step ladder. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE DESIGN: typeface cannot be the signal that separates caller-supplied text from system-derived text, so UntrustedField carries that distinction on fill, an amber rule and an explicit NOT VERIFIED caption instead. Those three survive and are unmistakable; the mono face does not exist here to be seen.

layout.$comment: The approval prompt is 420pt wide. Popover and menu-bar surfaces share the same width so the product reads as one system. windowWidth (720) is the console's window surfaces — the grants manager, the activity timeline and settings — which are wide enough for a grant row to state consequence, scope, holder, origin and life left on one line each. minWindowHeight is the smallest window the prompt is designed for, which is the referent B5's 'reason visible without scrolling' is measured against: the prompt MEASURES 710 tall (header 237 + body 236 + footer 238) and the reason sits at y=107-163 inside the NON-SCROLLING 237pt header, so it is visible at this height and at any taller one. Two earlier numbers were wrong: 560 was a guess 150pt short, and 704 was 6pt short. Measure the artifact, never the intent.
